name: mysql
description: Connect to a MySQL server with the mysql command-line client.

flags.description: Server hostname or IP (default localhost via socket)
Prompt for password; -pSECRET (no space) passes it inline
Unix socket file to connect through
TLS mode: DISABLED, PREFERRED, REQUIRED, VERIFY_CA, VERIFY_IDENTITY

examples.description: Connect to the local server as root and prompt for the password
Connect to a remote server and select the myapp database
Force an encrypted connection over TCP
Connect using credentials stored with mysql_config_editor

notes: Avoid -pSECRET on shared machines: the password is visible in shell history and process lists. Use -p alone or --login-path.
On Linux, "localhost" connects via the Unix socket; use -h 127.0.0.1 to force TCP.
Exit the client with \q, quit or exit.
mysql_native_password is disabled by default in MySQL 8.4 and removed in 9.0; old clients or drivers that only support it will fail to authenticate

name: mysql -e
description: Run SQL statements or a .sql file non-interactively from the shell.

flags.description: Continue executing a file even if an SQL error occurs

examples.description: Execute a SQL file against the myapp database
Run a single statement and exit

examples.command: mysql -u root -p -N -B -e "SELECT id, email FROM myapp.users" > users.tsv
examples.description: Export query results as tab-separated values without headers
Run a SQL file from inside an interactive mysql session

notes: End a statement with \G instead of ; inside the client to print rows vertically, which is easier to read for wide rows.

name: mysql_config_editor
description: Store connection credentials in an obfuscated login-path file so you don't type passwords.

examples.description: Save a login path named local (prompts for password)
List stored login paths (passwords are masked)
Delete a stored login path

notes: Credentials are stored in ~/.mylogin.cnf. The file is obfuscated, not encrypted, so keep its permissions restricted.
The login path also works with mysqldump, mysqladmin and mysqlcheck via --login-path.

name: mysql_secure_installation
description: Interactively harden a fresh MySQL install (root password, anonymous users, test database).

examples.description: Run the hardening wizard on a new server

notes: Removes anonymous users, disallows remote root login and drops the test database if you answer yes.

name: SHOW DATABASES
description: List all databases the current user can see.

examples.description: List all databases
Filter databases by name pattern

name: USE
description: Switch the default database for the current session.

examples.description: Make myapp the default database
Show which database is currently selected

name: CREATE DATABASE
description: Create a new database, optionally with a character set and collation.

examples.command: CREATE DATABASE myapp CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci;
examples.description: Create a database with full Unicode (emoji) support

examples.command: CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS myapp;
examples.description: Create only if it doesn't already exist
Show the charset and collation of an existing database

notes: Use utf8mb4, not utf8 (utf8mb3), which cannot store 4-byte characters like emoji.
utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci is the MySQL 8.0+ default collation; MariaDB does not support it.

name: DROP DATABASE
description: Permanently delete a database and all of its tables.

examples.description: Drop a database without erroring if it is missing

notes: WARNING: all tables and data are deleted immediately and cannot be rolled back. Take a mysqldump first.
Double-check the database name; there is no confirmation prompt.

name: SHOW TABLES
description: List tables (and optionally views) in the current or a named database.

examples.description: List tables in the current database
List tables in myapp matching a pattern
List only views

name: DESCRIBE
description: Show the columns, types, nullability, keys and defaults of a table.

examples.description: Show column definitions for the users table
Include collation, privileges and column comments
List indexes on the table

notes: DESC users; is a shorthand for DESCRIBE.

name: SHOW CREATE TABLE
description: Print the exact CREATE TABLE statement for a table, including indexes and engine.

examples.description: Show the DDL for users in vertical format

name: information_schema.TABLES
description: Query table sizes and row estimates from information_schema.

examples.command: SELECT table_name, ROUND((data_length + index_length) / 1024 / 1024, 1) AS size_mb FROM information_schema.TABLES WHERE table_schema = 'myapp' ORDER BY size_mb DESC;
examples.description: List the largest tables in myapp

examples.command: SELECT table_schema, ROUND(SUM(data_length + index_length) / 1024 / 1024, 1) AS size_mb FROM information_schema.TABLES GROUP BY table_schema;
examples.description: Total size per database

notes: TABLE_ROWS is an estimate for InnoDB tables; use SELECT COUNT(*) for an exact count.

name: CREATE USER
description: Create a new MySQL account for a given host.

examples.description: Create a user that can connect from any host
Create a user restricted to local connections

examples.command: SELECT user, host, plugin FROM mysql.user;
examples.description: List existing accounts and their auth plugin

notes: An account is user + host: 'app'@'localhost' and 'app'@'%' are different accounts.
MySQL 8.0+ defaults to caching_sha2_password. mysql_native_password is deprecated, disabled by default in 8.4 (enable with --mysql-native-password=ON) and removed in 9.0.

name: GRANT
description: Give privileges on databases or tables to an account.

examples.command: GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON myapp.* TO 'app_user'@'%';
examples.description: Full access to every table in myapp

examples.command: GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON myapp.* TO 'app_user'@'%';
examples.description: Typical read/write application access
Read-only access from a private subnet

notes: GRANT no longer creates users in MySQL 8.0+; run CREATE USER first.
FLUSH PRIVILEGES is not needed after GRANT/REVOKE; it is only required after editing the mysql.* grant tables directly.

name: REVOKE
description: Remove privileges from an account.

examples.description: Remove only the DELETE privilege

examples.command: REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES, GRANT OPTION FROM 'app_user'@'%';
examples.description: Strip every privilege from an account

name: SHOW GRANTS
description: Show the privileges assigned to an account.

examples.description: Show privileges for the current user
Show privileges for a specific account

name: ALTER USER
description: Change an account's password, authentication plugin or lock state.

examples.description: Change a user's password
Change your own password
Disable logins for an account without dropping it

examples.command: ALTER USER 'app_user'@'%' IDENTIFIED WITH caching_sha2_password BY '<new-password>';
examples.description: Move an account off mysql_native_password before upgrading to 9.x

examples.command: SELECT user, host FROM mysql.user WHERE plugin = 'mysql_native_password';
examples.description: Find accounts still using the legacy plugin

name: DROP USER
description: Delete a MySQL account and its privileges.

examples.description: Remove an account

notes: WARNING: applications using this account will immediately fail to connect.

name: EXPLAIN
description: Show the execution plan the optimizer will use for a query.

examples.command: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 42;
examples.description: Show the plan in tabular form (check type, key, rows)

examples.command: EXPLAIN FORMAT=TREE SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 42;
examples.description: Show the plan as a readable tree (8.0.16+)

examples.command: EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 42\G
examples.description: Detailed JSON plan with cost estimates

notes: type = ALL means a full table scan; look for a suitable index.
key shows which index was chosen; NULL means none.

name: EXPLAIN ANALYZE
description: Execute a query and report actual timings and row counts for each plan step.

examples.command: EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 42;
examples.description: Compare estimated vs actual rows and time per step

notes: Available in MySQL 8.0.18+.
WARNING: the query is actually executed; avoid running slow or data-modifying statements on production

name: SHOW PROCESSLIST
description: List active connections and the queries they are running.

examples.description: Show all connections with full query text

examples.command: SELECT id, user, host, db, time, state, info FROM information_schema.PROCESSLIST WHERE command <> 'Sleep' ORDER BY time DESC;
examples.description: Show only active queries, longest-running first
Cancel the running statement on connection 1234 but keep the connection
Terminate connection 1234 entirely

notes: Without the PROCESS privilege you only see your own threads.
Killing a long-running write may trigger a lengthy rollback.

name: SHOW VARIABLES
description: Inspect server configuration variables.

examples.description: Check a single setting
Show all buffer pool settings
Show global timeout settings

name: SHOW STATUS
description: Inspect server status counters such as connections, queries and buffer pool usage.

examples.description: Current number of open connections
Number of queries that exceeded long_query_time
Detailed InnoDB state including the latest deadlock

name: SET GLOBAL
description: Change a server variable at runtime, optionally persisting it across restarts.

examples.description: Change a setting until the next restart
Change a setting and persist it to mysqld-auto.cnf (8.0+)
Change a setting for the current connection only
Remove a persisted setting from mysqld-auto.cnf

notes: SET GLOBAL changes are lost on restart unless also added to my.cnf or set with SET PERSIST.
Requires SYSTEM_VARIABLES_ADMIN (or SUPER on older versions).

name: slow_query_log
description: Enable and analyze the slow query log to find expensive queries.

examples.description: Turn on the slow query log at runtime
Log queries taking longer than 1 second (applies to new connections)
Find where the log is written
Summarize the 10 slowest query patterns by total time

notes: Set log_queries_not_using_indexes = ON to also log full scans, but it can be noisy.
To keep the setting after a restart add slow_query_log = 1 and long_query_time to my.cnf.

name: sys schema
description: Use the built-in sys views to find slow statements, unused indexes and lock waits

examples.command: SELECT query, exec_count, total_latency FROM sys.statement_analysis LIMIT 10;
examples.description: Top statements by total latency
Statements that scan whole tables
Indexes not used since the server started
Indexes duplicated by another index
Who is blocking whom right now

notes: Built on performance_schema (enabled by default); statistics reset on restart, so check uptime before dropping "unused" indexes
x$ variants (e.g. sys.x$statement_analysis) return raw numbers instead of formatted values

name: SHOW REPLICA STATUS
description: Check replication health on a replica and start or stop the replication threads

examples.description: Show replica thread state, lag and last errors
Quick health check from the shell
Stop the receiver and applier threads
Start replication
On the source: list connected replicas

notes: Healthy: Replica_IO_Running = Yes, Replica_SQL_Running = Yes, and Seconds_Behind_Source low (NULL means not replicating)
SHOW SLAVE STATUS, START/STOP SLAVE, RESET SLAVE and SHOW SLAVE HOSTS were removed in MySQL 8.4; use the REPLICA forms
performance_schema.replication_connection_status and replication_applier_status_by_worker give the same data as queryable tables

name: CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE TO
description: Point a replica at its source server (replaces CHANGE MASTER TO)

examples.command: CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE TO SOURCE_HOST='source.example.com', SOURCE_PORT=3306, SOURCE_USER='repl', SOURCE_PASSWORD='<password>', SOURCE_AUTO_POSITION=1, SOURCE_SSL=1;
examples.description: Configure GTID-based replication over TLS

examples.command: CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE TO SOURCE_HOST='source.example.com', SOURCE_USER='repl', SOURCE_PASSWORD='<password>', SOURCE_LOG_FILE='binlog.000042', SOURCE_LOG_POS=157;
examples.description: Configure file/position-based replication
Keep a delayed replica one hour behind

examples.command: CREATE USER 'repl'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY '<password>'; GRANT REPLICATION SLAVE ON *.* TO 'repl'@'%';
examples.description: On the source: create the replication account

notes: Run STOP REPLICA first; connection options can't change while the receiver thread runs
CHANGE MASTER TO and the MASTER_* options were removed in MySQL 8.4; use SOURCE_* (e.g. SOURCE_HOST, SOURCE_LOG_POS)
With caching_sha2_password over a non-TLS link, add GET_SOURCE_PUBLIC_KEY=1
The privilege is still named REPLICATION SLAVE

name: SHOW BINARY LOG STATUS
description: Inspect and purge binary logs on a source server (replaces SHOW MASTER STATUS)

examples.description: Current binary log file, position and executed GTID set
List binary log files and their sizes

examples.command: PURGE BINARY LOGS BEFORE NOW() - INTERVAL 7 DAY;
examples.description: Delete binary logs older than 7 days
Expire binary logs automatically after 7 days

notes: SHOW MASTER STATUS, SHOW MASTER LOGS, PURGE MASTER LOGS and RESET MASTER were removed in MySQL 8.4; RESET MASTER is now RESET BINARY LOGS AND GTIDS
WARNING: don't purge logs that a replica (or point-in-time recovery) still needs; check SHOW REPLICA STATUS on every replica first
WARNING: RESET BINARY LOGS AND GTIDS deletes every binary log and clears GTID history

name: mysqldump
description: Create a logical SQL backup of one or more databases.

flags.description: Consistent snapshot for InnoDB without locking tables
Dump several named databases and include CREATE DATABASE statements
Data only, no CREATE TABLE statements
Stream rows instead of buffering whole tables (on by default via --opt)
Omit GTID statements, useful when restoring onto a server with different GTIDs
Record the binary log position as a comment (replaces the deprecated --master-data)

examples.description: Consistent backup of one InnoDB database without locking tables
Compressed, dated backup
Back up every database on the server
Dump the schema only, no rows

examples.command: mysqldump -u root -p myapp users orders > tables.sql
examples.description: Dump only specific tables

notes: --single-transaction only gives a consistent snapshot for InnoDB tables; MyISAM tables can still change during the dump.
Without --databases, the dump has no CREATE DATABASE/USE, so you must name the target database when restoring.
For large databases, consider MySQL Shell's util.dumpInstance(), which is parallel and much faster. mysqlpump was removed in MySQL 8.4; use mysqldump or MySQL Shell instead.

name: mysql < dump.sql
description: Restore a database from a mysqldump file.

examples.description: Restore into an existing database named myapp
Restore from a gzip-compressed dump
Restore a dump made with --all-databases or --databases

notes: Create the target database first if the dump was made without --databases.
WARNING: restoring overwrites tables that exist in the dump (it includes DROP TABLE IF EXISTS by default)

name: LOAD DATA
description: Bulk-import a CSV or TSV file into a table

examples.command: LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE 'users.csv' INTO TABLE users FIELDS TERMINATED BY ',' ENCLOSED BY '"' LINES TERMINATED BY '\n' IGNORE 1 LINES (name, email, created_at);
examples.description: Import a CSV with a header row from the client machine
Start the client with LOCAL file loading allowed
Allow LOCAL loading on the server
Check whether the server allows LOCAL loading

notes: LOCAL reads the file from the client; without LOCAL the file must be on the server and inside secure_file_priv
local_infile is OFF by default; both server and client must allow it
Much faster than row-by-row INSERTs for large files; use LINES TERMINATED BY '\r\n' for Windows files

name: mysqlsh
description: MySQL Shell: an advanced client with SQL, JavaScript and Python modes plus parallel dump/load utilities.

examples.description: Connect in SQL mode
Parallel dump of the whole instance (run in JS mode)
Load a dump created by dumpInstance/dumpSchemas (JS mode)
Check an instance for problems before upgrading to the next LTS (e.g. 8.4 to 9.7)

notes: Installed separately from the server (package mysql-shell).
Switch modes inside the shell with \sql, \js or \py.
util.loadDump requires local_infile=ON on the target server.

name: mysqladmin
description: Perform server administration tasks such as health checks and shutdown from the shell.

examples.description: Show uptime, threads, queries and slow query count
Check whether the server is alive (prints "mysqld is alive")
Show running threads
Dump all global status counters
Cleanly shut down the server

notes: shutdown stops the server for every client; prefer systemctl stop mysql on systemd hosts so the service manager stays in sync.

name: mysqlcheck
description: Check, analyze, optimize or repair tables while the server is running.

examples.description: Check all tables in all databases for errors
Refresh index statistics for the optimizer
Rebuild a table to reclaim space

notes: --repair does not work on InnoDB tables.
--optimize on InnoDB rebuilds the table, which can take a long time and lots of disk on large tables.

name: systemctl mysql
description: Start, stop and check the MySQL server service on systemd-based Linux.

examples.description: Check whether the server is running (service is mysqld on RHEL/Fedora)
Restart the server to apply my.cnf changes
View recent server log entries
Restart MySQL installed with Homebrew on macOS

notes: The service is called mysql on Debian/Ubuntu and mysqld on RHEL, Fedora and Oracle Linux.
mysql_upgrade was removed in 8.4: the server upgrades the data dictionary and system tables automatically on startup
